title: Biomarkers of Early Stress Experiences in Cerebrospinal Fluid of Pregnant Women at the Time of Delivery
summary:
This study serves, first, to establish a procedure for recruiting participants and for collecting cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for research purposes in the context of a planned cesarean section. This approach enables the collection of data with high potential to advance our field that would otherwise be inaccessible due to the invasiveness of CSF sampling. Because sample collection is linked to the administration of medically indicated spinal anesthesia, participation does not entail any additional risk to the participant as a result of CSF collection. This study is intended to prepare a larger-scale study on maternal programming in the context of early life stress experiences.

Second, the study may already provide initial indications of neurobiological mechanisms in the maternal brain that could underlie the intergenerational effects of early life stress.

interventions.name:
1. General procedure

This is a feasibility study in a population-based sample of 50 pregnant women with a planned delivery by cesarean section (primary cesarean) due to minor complications (e.g., previous cesarean delivery, breech presentation of the fetus) or personal preference.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
a) Planned cesarean section (primary cesarean) due to personal preference or minor complications, i.e., cesarean section in a previous pregnancy, breech presentation, uncomplicated placenta previa
b) Age ≥ 18 years
c) Sufficient proficiency in the German language
d) Singleton pregnancy
e) Gestational age ≥ 37 weeks at delivery
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria:
a) Current medication that markedly dysregulates the production or function of the measured parameters (e.g., steroids, non-steroidal analgesics/NSAIDs, tocolytics, antidepressants)
b) Current diagnosed depressive episode
c) Alcohol and substance abuse
d) Diagnosed fetal anomalies or severe illness of the newborn
